hint.text: Producing and consuming clothing in this way is called fast fashion.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.b: It is important to think about sustainability when shopping for ((++clothes clouds)). Buying lots of cheap, mass-produced clothes that will soon need replacing ((++harms helps)) the environment.

This is because producing so much clothing uses up the Earth’s ((++natural naughty)) resources. When the clothes are thrown away, they end up in ((++landfills waterfills)) or are burned, polluting the planet.

instruction.text: It’s also important to shop for food sustainably. Read the tips and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Use reusable shopping bags instead of plastic bags.
Buy fruit and vegetables that aren’t packaged in plastic.
Check that items have recycling labels before buying them.

instruction.text: Decide whether the following statements are true or false.

atoms.a: Growing your own food is a lot less harmful to the environment than buying them from the supermarket.
Buying locally-grown, in-season products is more sustainable than buying imported products.
Buying fruit and vegetables without plastic packaging is worse for the environment.

instruction.text: Another way to practise sustainability is to change your diet to consume fewer meat products. Read the conversation and fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Hi Toni! I know that you’re a ((++vegetarian giraffe)), but what does that mean?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'>Hi Toni! I know that you’re a vegetarian, but what does that mean?</prosody>

atoms.b: A vegetarian is someone who doesn’t eat any ((vegetables ++meat)) or its by-products, such as gelatin, which is made from animal ((++fat hair)).
Why did you choose to be a vegetarian?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'>Why did you choose to be a vegetarian?</prosody>

atoms.b: For me, having a vegetarian diet is one of the ways that I practise ((++sustainability recycling)).

Animals like cows and chickens produce a gas called ((++methane gasoline)), which pollutes the atmosphere. So, by not consuming meat products, I am not contributing to ((++greenhouse bluehouse)) gas emissions.
